calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if a deadline is < 90 days from 2026-11-13, otherwise High/Medium/Low by importance), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

items.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride
items.reason: FDA final order removes methylene chloride, trichloroethylene and ethylene dichloride as extraction solvents for annatto, paprika and turmeric oleoresin colors, which may be used in our hot dogs, sausages and candy; it takes effect 2027-01-11. A secondary source gives 2026-12-12 as the comment/objection date.
items.action: Maria Chen: ask color suppliers to confirm in writing that annatto, paprika and turmeric colors are made without these solvents, and file any objections or comments by 12/12.

items.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene
items.reason: FDA final order, issued under the Delaney Clause, revokes methylene chloride as a diluent in inks that mark fruit and vegetables, effective 2027-01-11. It also denies the petition's other requests. Our direct exposure is low and limited to marked fruit, such as apples we buy.
items.action: Maria Chen: confirm with Tom Alvarez that no apple suppliers use methylene chloride marking inks, and note the effective date in the color additive compliance file.

items.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
items.reason: USDA proposes limiting SNAP categorical eligibility to households receiving TANF assistance. Fewer households would qualify, which could cut SNAP-funded purchases at the grocery and convenience customers we sell through.
items.action: Aisha Grant: model the SNAP-revenue exposure by customer, decide whether to comment directly or through a trade group by 12/10, and brief leadership on the demand risk.

items.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
items.reason: USDA AMS proposes changes to the pecan marketing order (Order 986): sheller seats on the American Pecan Council, a new inter-handler transfer report, and late fees and interest on unpaid assessments. These could affect our pecan suppliers and any handler duties we have. The comment date comes from a secondary source.
items.action: Tom Alvarez: check whether we or our pecan suppliers act as handlers, review the new reporting and late-fee terms, and submit comments by 12/9 if warranted.
